 Mosses & Allied Plants of Southern Australia


freubia tasmanica              Treubiaceae                                             rv
Although this seems to be a very rare species, it is immediately recognisable because of
its distinctive thallus structure. It grows on open damp clay banks in upland forests,
usually creeping among grasses, herbs or lichens. Occasionally it is found on exposed
wet rock in streams. The vividly green thallus, up to 60 mm long and 8 mm wide, is
thick and fleshy but quite brittle. It is anchored to the soil by many colourless rhizoids.
The lobes are rather circular and resemble leaves, arranged regularly on each side of the
thallus. On the dorsal side are two rows of crescent-shaped, scale-like lobes, in the axils
of which may sometimes be found small yellow-green gemmae. The whole appearance
is therefore like a fleshy, leafy liverwort. As far as we know, sporophytes have never
been found.
     T lacunosa ('f) is immediately distinguishable because the thallus is covered in
minute yellow dots. These are cells that contain large oil bodies.

Similar species: Lethocolea pansa

Balantiopsie; diplophylla Balantiopsidaceae                                   WSTVN
This is a common species on soil in damp habitats, such as
south­facing road cuttings in wet forest. It can also form large
clumps in or on the edges of clear-flowing streams. The soft
shoots are pale fawn to green, reddish green or even purple.
The spined leaves are bilobed, with the smaller lobe lying flat on      diplophylla
the dorsal side of the leaf. Underleaves are well toothed and
deeply bifid.
     In H tumida (TVN) the leaves have two apical teeth on both
lobe and lobule, sometimes with a few extra small teeth. It grows
in bogs, swamps and other wet places, especially in alpine areas.
The illustration shows two forms with the leaves opened out,
and the corresponding underleaves.
     Diplophyllum domesticum (TVN) has the same leaf form,
but the margins are neither lobed nor toothed, although crenulate. It
occurs in much the same habitats as Balantiopsis. D.                       tumida
verrucosum (TVN) is an alpine species with a relatively much
larger lobule, about three-quarters of the size of the lobe. The
other southern Australian members of this genus in Australia are
all rare species from Tasmania: D. androgyhum, D. angustifolium,
D. dioicum, and D. incrassatum .                                        D. domesticum

Similar species: Schistochila spp.

WIKIPEDIA  (1) 
Treubia lacunosa is a species of liverwort in the family Treubiaceae that is found across New Zealand in moist shady areas on logs or soil. The organism is relatively complex for a liverwort, and hosts endosymbiotic fungi which provide it with growth-inhibiting nutrients.
